mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discounting of expected future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during tightening episodes (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 4% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market softness reduces growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while CPIAUCSL decreases in the same month
regime_hint: labor market cooling with deflationary pressures
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative despite the combined signal in >70% of similar episodes (backtest failure).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 5% from the prior month's level precedes a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return by signaling stronger near-term demand for goods.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive when INDPRO rises >5% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive 2-month decline in residential housing starts (HOUST) predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects weak building activity and reduced economic momentum.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative during periods of two consecutive HOUST declines (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4% for the first time in a month, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be positive due to reduced recession risk.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% in the current month
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly positive during such UNRATE breaks (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in both retail sales (not available in evidence) and industrial production (INDPRO) would predict a positive 20-day return, but using only INDPRO as proxy, a two-month rise in INDPRO triggers a positive 20-day return via momentum transfer.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rises for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not positive when INDPRO shows two-month up-trend (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) below the prior month's level in a labor market cooling regime is associated with a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return due to increased recession risk.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls in the current month during a cooling regime
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not negative when PAYEMS declines in cooling regimes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly ratio of demand (RSAFS) to supply (INDPRO) exceeds 1.2 for the first time, the S&P 20-day forward return is predicted to be negative, reflecting market anticipation of supply-side imbalance.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS/INDPRO ratio crosses above 1.2 in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negative when the ratio crosses 1.2 (p > 0.05).
